name: Attabad Lake
description: Surreal turquoise lake formed by the 2010 landslide. Jet-ski rentals and cafés on the KKH side.

name: Passu Cones Viewpoint
description: The cathedral ridge every KKH photo is famous for. Best light is early morning from the highway pullout.

name: Hussaini Suspension Bridge
description: Missing-plank rope bridge over the Hunza River. Not for the faint-hearted, and not for bikes.

name: Eagle's Nest, Duikar
description: Highest viewpoint above Hunza. Sunrise over Rakaposhi, Ultar and Ladyfinger in one sweep.

name: Rakaposhi View Point, Ghulmat
description: Roadside deck staring straight at a 7,788 m face. Stop for chai, stay for the glacier stream.

name: Baltit Fort, Karimabad
description: 700-year-old fort restored by the Aga Khan Trust. Rooftop views down the whole valley.

name: Altit Fort
description: Older sibling of Baltit, with the Royal Garden below. Quieter and worth the walk.

name: Borith Lake
description: Shallow brackish lake above Gulmit. Migratory birds in spring, easy tent pitches on the shore.

name: Khunjerab Pass
description: The highest paved border crossing on earth at 4,693 m. Thin air, yaks, and a gate to China.

name: Sost Dry Port
description: Last reliable fuel before Khunjerab. Fill up here — there is nothing above this point.

name: Café de Hunza, Karimabad
description: Walnut cake and Hunza coffee. The unofficial checkpoint for every rider heading north.

name: Glacier Breeze Restaurant, Gulmit
description: Apricot juice and Hunza bread served beside a glacial stream, right off the KKH.

name: Hard Rock Hunza Hotel
description: Cliff-edge rooms over the valley. Secure bike parking in the courtyard.

name: HBL ATM, Karimabad
description: One of the last dependable ATMs going north. Carry cash beyond Aliabad.

name: Passu Spring Water Point
description: Free glacier-fed spring tap by the roadside. Cold enough to hurt.

name: Gilgit City Centre
description: Regional hub for permits, spares, SIM cards and a real bed before the high passes.

name: Naltar Blue Lakes
description: Pine forest and impossibly blue lakes. Jeep track only — leave the road bike in Gilgit.

name: DHQ Hospital Gilgit
description: Largest hospital in Gilgit-Baltistan. Trauma care and oxygen available.

name: Jutial Bike Mechanic, Gilgit
description: Knows Chinese 150s and Honda CGs cold. Tyres, chains, sprockets in stock.

name: Attock Petroleum, Gilgit
description: Reliable high-octane. Top off before Nagar or the Skardu road.

name: Jamia Masjid Gilgit
description: Central mosque with wudu facilities and shaded parking.

name: Jaglot Check Post
description: Register your ID here. Keep photocopies of your CNIC handy for the whole KKH.

name: Three Mountains Junction
description: Where the Karakoram, Himalaya and Hindu Kush meet, above the Indus–Gilgit confluence.

name: Fairy Meadows
description: Alpine meadow facing the Nanga Parbat Rupal face. Jeep to Tato, then a 3-hour hike.

name: Nanga Parbat Base Camp Trail
description: Beyal Camp onward to base camp. Killer Mountain at arm’s length. Guide strongly advised.

name: Raikot Bridge Checkpost
description: Turn-off for Fairy Meadows. Jeeps wait here; leave your bike with the parking wallah.

name: Chilas Bazaar
description: Hot, dusty and unavoidable. Standard overnight stop between Naran and Gilgit.

name: PSO Fuel Station, Chilas
description: Fill here before Babusar or the Diamer stretch. Cash preferred.

name: DHQ Hospital Chilas
description: Basic emergency care on the Diamer stretch. Nearest real hospital is Gilgit.

name: Panorama Hotel Dhaba, Chilas
description: Cheap dal, cold drinks, and shade. Rider-friendly at odd hours.

name: Babusar Top
description: The 4,173 m gateway between Kaghan and the KKH. Usually open July–September only.

name: Babusar Top Chai Stall
description: Tin-shack tea at 4,000 m. Warms your hands and your decision-making.

name: Babusar Police Post
description: Confirms whether the pass is open. Ask before committing to the climb.

name: Lulusar Lake
description: Source of the Kunhar River. Dead-calm water right beside the road.

name: Lulusar Spring Refill
description: Roadside spring above the lake. Fill bottles before the Babusar climb.

name: Lake Saif ul Malook
description: Glacial lake under Malika Parbat. Jeep track from Naran is rough but rideable in summer.

name: Naran Bazaar
description: Basecamp for the whole valley. Hotels, spares, and traffic every summer weekend.

name: Shell Fuel Station, Naran
description: Last proper pump before Babusar Top. Expect a queue on weekends.

name: Naran Auto Workshop
description: Puncture repair and brake work. Handy after the descent from the lake track.

name: HBL ATM, Naran
description: Frequently out of cash in peak season. Withdraw in Mansehra as a backup.

name: Jamia Masjid Naran
description: Central mosque in the bazaar with parking on the Kunhar side.

name: Shogran Meadow
description: Pine plateau above Kiwai. Gentle enough for a first mountain camp.

name: Siri Paye Meadows
description: Rolling green shelf above Shogran. 4x4 or a very committed dirt rider only.

name: Kaghan Town
description: Trout and paratha halfway up the valley. Quieter than Naran.

name: THQ Hospital Balakot
description: First real medical stop coming down the Kaghan valley.

name: Skardu City
description: Gateway to K2, Deosai and Shigar. Best gear shops east of Gilgit.

name: Deosai Plains (Bara Pani)
description: The Land of Giants at 4,100 m. Brown bears, no trees, and nights that bite in August.

name: Sheosar Lake, Deosai
description: Mirror lake on the Deosai plateau with Nanga Parbat on the skyline.

name: Lower Kachura (Shangrila)
description: Heart-shaped lake with the old aircraft restaurant. Touristy but genuinely pretty.

name: Upper Kachura Lake
description: Deeper, colder and much quieter than its lower neighbour. Trout on the grill.

name: Katpana Cold Desert
description: Sand dunes at 2,200 m with snow peaks behind them. Ride at golden hour.

name: Shigar Fort
description: Restored 17th-century fort turned heritage hotel on the way to Askole.

name: Khaplu Palace
description: "Little Tibet" — the quiet end of Baltistan, with the Shyok River below.

name: CMH Skardu
description: Best-equipped medical facility in Baltistan. Altitude sickness treatment available.

name: NBP ATM, Skardu
description: Main bazaar ATM. Withdraw everything you need for Deosai here.

name: Kalam Valley
description: Riverside hotels and the jump-off for Mahodand and Ushu. Roads improve every year.

name: Mahodand Lake
description: Alpine lake past Ushu. The 35 km track from Kalam is rough, wet and worth it.

name: Kumrat Valley
description: Deodar forest, wooden huts and the Panjkora River. Camping culture at its best.

name: Malam Jabba
description: Pakistan's ski resort. Chairlift, zipline, and a paved climb that's fun on two wheels.

name: Mingora, Swat
description: Full spares market — the last place to fix anything properly before Kalam.

name: Shandur Pass
description: Roof of the World polo ground at 3,700 m. The Gilgit–Chitral crossing is pure adventure riding.

name: Chitral Town
description: Hindu Kush hub below Tirich Mir. Reload here before Kalash or Shandur.

name: Bumburet, Kalash Valley
description: Kalash heartland. Permits required; respect the local customs and festivals.

name: Lowari Tunnel
description: 10 km tunnel replacing the old pass. Lights on, visor up — it is wet and unlit in stretches.

name: Ratti Gali Lake
description: Alpine lake above Dowarian. 4x4 to base, then a hard hike. Snow lingers into July.

name: Arang Kel
description: Meadow village above Kel, reached by chairlift then a steep climb. Phones barely work.

name: Keran, Neelum Valley
description: Riverside huts facing the LoC. Beautiful, but keep to marked areas.

name: Kohala Bridge
description: Historic bridge on the Muzaffarabad–Murree road where the Jhelum enters Azad Kashmir. Gateway to Neelum Valley.

name: Sharda, Neelum Valley
description: Ancient university ruins and riverside meadows at the far end of Neelum. Worth the long ride from Muzaffarabad.

name: Taobat Bala
description: Last major settlement before the Line of Control in upper Neelum. Pine forests, cold streams, minimal traffic.

name: Kel, Neelum Valley
description: Base camp for Arang Kel and upper Neelum. Chairlift, basic hotels, and the road narrows from here.

name: Dowarian
description: Jump-off for Ratti Gali Lake trek. Tent pitches by the river, 4x4 tracks heading uphill.

name: Athmuqam
description: District HQ on the Neelum road. Last proper supplies before Kel and Sharda.

name: Banjosa Lake, Rawalakot
description: Pine-ringed artificial lake. Easy weekend target from Islamabad.

name: Nathia Gali
description: Cool pine air two hours from Islamabad. Mukshpuri trailhead starts in town.

name: Ayubia National Park
description: Pipeline Track through moist temperate forest. Monkeys will absolutely raid your panniers.

name: Murree Mall Road
description: Crowded, kitsch, and still the default first mountain trip for most Pakistani riders.

name: Faisal Mosque, Islamabad
description: Margalla backdrop, huge courtyard. Common meet-up point for group departures.

name: Pir Sohawa, Margalla Hills
description: Switchbacks up Margalla with the city laid out below. Perfect shakedown ride.

name: Total Fuel Station, Mansehra
description: Where the KKH run really begins. Air, oil and a clean washroom.

name: Mansehra Tyre & Tube
description: Tube swaps in ten minutes. Ask them to check your chain tension too.

name: PSO Besham
description: Mid-point of the Hazara–Chilas grind. Sketchy after dark, fine by day.

name: Dassu Checkpost
description: Kohistan stretch registration. Foreign riders may need an escort here.

name: Khewra Salt Mine
description: Second-largest salt mine on earth. Easy detour off the M2 heading south.

name: Khabeki Lake, Soon Valley
description: Punjab's overlooked salt-range valley. Empty roads, flamingos in winter.

name: Badshahi Mosque, Lahore
description: Mughal masterpiece by the Walled City. Classic start line for southbound rides.

name: Fort Munro
description: Punjab's only hill station, on the Sulaiman range above DG Khan. Great switchbacks.

name: Kund Malir Beach
description: Desert meets ocean on the Makran Coastal Highway. Camp behind the dunes.

name: Princess of Hope, Hingol
description: Wind-carved rock figure in Hingol National Park. Mud volcanoes nearby.

name: Gwadar Hammerhead
description: Cliff plateau over the Arabian Sea. 600 km of empty coastal highway to get here.

name: Ziarat Juniper Forest
description: One of the oldest juniper forests in the world. Freezing nights, brilliant stars.

name: Hanna Lake, Quetta
description: Turquoise reservoir in the Urak valley just outside Quetta.

name: Clifton Seaview, Karachi
description: Where every Makran coastal run starts or ends. Late-night food guaranteed.
